Changelog

Each release leads with one change, then a few fixes.

v2.5.22026-11-26

Fixes false timeouts during long managed runs, broken Antigravity tool card rendering, and non-working long-context toggles.

  • Renew the managed main-chat observation deadline on runtime progress and probe live runtime state when idle, so multi-step tool runs or long reasoning turns over 2 minutes no longer abort with an observation timeout.
  • Fix Antigravity (ACP) tool display: classify `run_shell_command` with summaries, parse PascalCase tool arguments, fall back to `rawOutput`, and preserve `write_file` / whole-file edit diffs.
  • Restore long-context and reasoning-effort toggles in managed conversations for both the Nomi runtime and third-party models on managed CLI runtimes.

Details

  • Managed Nomi agent traces now accumulate raw tool arguments in `Detail` and truncate outputs along valid UTF-8 boundaries instead of slicing mid-character.
  • Raised the per-turn active trace cap and ACP / dsh runtime event channel buffers to 512 to prevent drops during tool-heavy turns.
  • Managed conversations now skip legacy `store.updateMeta` writes for queued sends and lock the project picker to avoid conflicting metadata updates.

v2.5.12026-11-25

Fixes the changed-files popover closing early and intercepting `Esc` shortcuts from the composer.

  • Keep the changed-files popover open while either keyboard focus or pointer hover remains on the trigger pill or file list, so crossing the gap to scroll the list no longer dismisses it.
  • Handle `Esc` dismissal in the bubbling phase and ignore IME composition, so hovering the summary pill no longer swallows the chat input's own `Esc` shortcuts.

Details

  • The 180ms pointer-leave delay clears only the pointer state so keyboard focus keeps the popover open, and moving focus away while still hovering keeps it open as well.
  • Clicking outside the popover or picking a file to open the side-by-side Diff workbench still closes the popover immediately.

v2.5.02026-11-25

Pick a base per conversation in the main chat and talk straight through an installed official CLI — no third-party provider setup first.

  • Pick an installed official CLI as the base for each main-chat conversation — Claude Code, Codex and the other built-in CLIs — without configuring a third-party model provider.
  • Switch bases within the same conversation; switching back resumes that CLI's own session and only sends what happened while you were away, falling back to a new session with a bounded full handoff only when it cannot resume, and asking you to choose when recovery is unknown.
  • Cancel a running turn, approve or reject tool calls one by one, and retry a failed or interrupted request as the same request without it being merged into the next one.
  • First-use onboarding lets you pick a local CLI whose executable was detected as your default base for later conversations; CLIs with no executable are shown with their status but cannot be picked. The managed runtime states which capabilities are available, and unsupported ones such as attachments or knowledge-base questions are refused before sending instead of being dropped silently.
  • A new OpenCode Go preset under Settings → Models & Providers → Third-party providers, ready to use once you enter your subscription key, with model discovery.
  • API-backed managed conversations now have tools too: choose a permission mode per conversation and tool actions run with your confirmation, and switching to "allow everything" asks for confirmation before it skips per-action prompts.
  • Antigravity can sign in and out of its local official account inside the app; in-app login management is only offered for CLIs that declare the capability, which today is Antigravity alone. Other CLIs still sign in through their own CLI. Sign-in is not checked here and stays with each CLI — a CLI that is not signed in reports that itself.
  • Preview: ignore files such as `.gitignore`, common config files such as `Dockerfile`, `Makefile` and `nginx.conf` are highlighted by file name, YAML keys and unquoted values plus JSON keys and CSS properties now have colours, the tab bar scrolls horizontally with the mouse wheel, and the changed-files popover is no longer covered by the chat sidebar.

Details

  • MiniMax Code updates in the app no longer stay on the old version: the received version is checked after updating, other methods are tried if it did not move, and a failure is reported with logs kept.
  • Fixed a data race in delegation when a background task finishes or is cancelled: the sporadic race is gone, background slots are still returned, and a cancellation still reaches the right tab.
  • Fixed CLI-only entry in onboarding: picking a local CLI does not finish onboarding or switch conversations, it only sets the default base for later ones.
  • Boundary: this release implements Windows durable writes and process-tree management and passes cross-compilation, but has not been verified on native Windows yet; the official CLIs were not exercised on a real installed-and-signed-in setup either, and those paths are covered by protocol-level stand-in processes. Please confirm on your own system.

v2.4.22026-11-20

Drag files straight into the composer, toggle long context per chat, and open run traces as dockable workspace tabs.

  • Drag files from the sidebar file tree, changed-file list, git status or preview tab menu into the composer and their paths are inserted as `@path` at the cursor. The file tree and preview tab menu can copy paths too.
  • Long context is no longer switched on automatically: toggle it from the model menu or the context ring in the composer, which shows the standard window, maximum input and surcharge. The choice is remembered per chat and per model, and side chats, forks and compacted histories keep it.
  • Run traces can open as dockable workspace tabs, scoped to a whole chat or a single turn, with graph, timeline, thinking and model audit views. Session details gain a traces entry, and opening a trace from the chat brings that turn's question into the title.
  • The task board can archive finished tasks, all of them at once if you like. New tasks queue up with the reason shown when the board is full, and requests that need your decision appear as "Awaiting confirmation".
  • A long-running Nomi turn can be handed off to a background task from the chat with "Move to background" or `/bg`, returning you to the conversation right away.
  • Session details gain a Terminals section listing each terminal, its status and working directory, with a click to focus it.
  • Preview now has find and replace: case sensitive, whole word and regex, next and previous, single or replace all, and your last query is remembered. Markdown, text and diffs all work.
  • Clicking "Open" on a notification in the dynamic island switches to the matching chat or task first, then activates the window and jumps there instead of staying on the current tab.

Details

  • Queued messages can carry images alone. After a restart, a queued message whose images were not saved is marked "Attachments missing" and paused, and you can re-attach images, switch to text only or delete it; failed messages can be retried with one click.
  • Removing a project now takes effect the first time, with the same confirmation wording as the sidebar and moved chats listed under "Other chats".
  • The chat column and side column now split by ratio (50:50 by default, each limited to 20%–80%) and remember the ratio. The floating sidebar no longer pushes the title bar aside and keeps its narrow width while leaving.
  • CLI launchers resolve from PATH and the usual install folders, with detection and launching sharing one resolver. On Windows, npm's lowercase shims (such as `reclaude.cmd`) are found on case-sensitive hosts, so login detection and usage queries use the same CLI as the chat.
  • Sidebar status dots only turn green when a turn truly finishes, with distinct colours for failures and manual stops. The asset library lists generated images only and no longer collects images you send.
  • Endpoint usage information is reused across the asset library, CLI install state and settings, cutting repeat requests and the empty flash on first open, and closing the getting-started card on an empty chat unmounts it.
  • On macOS the floating island responds to the first click while inactive, and in the built-in browser links you trigger open in the current view while script-opened popups are blocked.
  • The delegation confirmation shows the permission mode actually used along with sandbox and working-directory protections, so you know what is being opened up.
  • Returning a popped-out tab to the main window now uses a request/confirmation handshake, so content is kept if the main window does not respond.

v2.4.12026-11-19

The side workspace now has a built-in terminal, empty Agent chats guide you to pick a model, and gateway failover is off by default until you turn it on.

  • The side workspace gains a built-in interactive terminal: each tab reuses the same session and replays recent output, and you can split the pane, clear the screen, change directory, restart, or open it in the system terminal. Closing a pane or tab that still has a running process asks first. The new-tab page is now grouped entry cards for "Workspace" and "Collaboration & tools", and terminals open at the project's primary folder.
  • An empty Agent chat no longer fails on the first message when no model or account is set. A card above the composer lets you choose a model or jump to settings, and sending runs a configuration check first.
  • Circuit breaking and failover are now a switch, off by default. While it is off, a failure is reported as-is and the gateway does not switch to another provider. Turn it on at the top right of Settings → Models & Agents → Third-Party Providers if you want automatic failover.
  • The "Third-Party Models" tab is now "Third-Party Providers". A third-party model that natively belongs to the running CLI inherits that CLI's own thinking level, and the picker shows "Default".
  • Queued messages can now carry images, with thumbnails in the pending list and a new "Stop and send" action. If delivery fails, the text and images stay at the front with a visible reason and a Retry button, instead of disappearing.
  • Background delegations finish with a brief toast instead of stacking chat bubbles. When an in-place card is already on screen, the result is still available to the model on the next turn. Multiple CLIs of the same type get a stable short name so you can tell them apart.
  • The sidebar's local-history section now starts expanded, and scrolling to the bottom loads the next page automatically. Long conversations no longer jump while scrolling, and a turn quick-nav rail runs alongside the thread.
  • Creating a new chat on the other CLI endpoints now reuses an existing untouched chat in the same project, instead of opening another tab every time.

Details

  • Oversized pastes into the built-in terminal are written in character-safe chunks instead of being dropped silently. If a chunk fails, a visible error is shown and the remainder is not retried automatically, so half a command is not run twice.
  • Empty Agent tabs reconcile their source and model after sign-in or catalog changes, and wait for an explicit choice instead of silently picking the first provider when several are configured without a default. Switching away discards the previous never-used empty tab.
  • Delegated child agents always run in automatic mode, so they no longer stall on a permission prompt just because Nomi itself is in a manual mode. Unsupported permission modes on the other end fall back to default, and permission requests are not answered twice.
  • Newer Claude adaptive thinking is sent as adaptive, without a fixed token budget. Claude and Codex startup settings also follow the native model more closely.
  • Inline file links resolve more reliably. The project dialog disables Delete while a removal is in flight, and Seed no longer creates a second project for the same directory when one path is a symlink.
  • Agent cards no longer overflow at narrow widths, and the close button stays pinned on the right. The close button on a tab is no longer treated as a drag handle.
  • The "Back to chat" row is removed from the top of the settings sidebar; Esc still closes settings. The tab strips are quieter: top-level tabs use background color only, and file tabs move their selection bar to the bottom edge.
  • The built-in Windows terminal is more reliable: the child shell's ordinary stdout/stderr could go to the host's own console instead of the pseudoconsole, so the in-app terminal missed the prompt. The child is now started with empty standard handles (`STARTF_USESTDHANDLES`), the same pattern Microsoft's ConPTY tests use, so its output stays on the pseudoconsole. The released desktop binary is built with `-H windowsgui` and usually has no host console, so this mainly matters for CI, debug or console-hosted runs, and any host that already has a console.

v2.4.02026-11-18

Settings → "Models & Agents" is reorganized, default routing now follows the model source, and an interjection mid-reply splits the current turn into a new stage.

  • Merge the old Models and coding-agent settings into "Models & Agents", with tabs for Task & cost routing, Agents & accounts, Third-party models, Local models, and Monitoring & sessions. Third-party and local models no longer share one long page, and the old deep links still open the matching tab.
  • Derive default routing from the model source: local sign-in, official accounts, local models and the gateway can coexist, each with its own fallback. If no CLI is available, the default falls back to Nomi. The picker only lists sources you can actually use.
  • Rename the Chinese UI term for coding assistants to "agent"; section titles stay "Agents", "CLI Agents" and "Agents & accounts".
  • When you interject mid-reply, the turn splits into independent stages. In the Minimal view each stage folds on its own, with its own step count and timer, and the status follows the active stage.
  • Scheduled tasks that target a preset now save only the preset, so the current preset is used at trigger time. The runner picker reads the model catalog for the selected source (local sign-in or official account) instead of showing the other side's models.
  • Use the configured custom launcher for login detection and quota queries, instead of inferring a wrapper's auth from the native CLI's config. On Windows, wrapper names such as reclaude resolve to reclaude.cmd on probe paths. Thanks to Assassin-Q.
  • Fix the light-theme canvas color leaking into the other six themes; it now applies to the light theme only.

Details

  • If a preset is deleted or cannot be resolved, the task fails and asks you to pick a preset again, instead of running the previously saved agent. After a preset switches agents, tab reuse only looks at tabs of the same agent.
  • When a resumed run's execution settings no longer match the previous preset, the message says the work is kept in the working directory and to restore the previous preset settings and choose Continue, or start a new task. It no longer names a specific agent or hints at sending credentials.
  • Model controls, the sidebar, the composer and session details follow the selected source. Multiple sources can coexist, each with its own fallback.

v2.3.182026-11-17

Browser tabs now sit in the conversation window as a native child view, so external pages can actually open. Chats are also less likely to lose messages if the app restarts mid-reply.

  • Embed a browser tab's page as a native child view of the conversation window, instead of an iframe or a separate window. Sites that used to refuse embedding, such as Google and GitHub, now open, and the page no longer floats over settings and dialogs.
  • Add a "Minimal" conversation detail mode and make it the default for new setups: collapsed, it shows step progress, elapsed time and the final summary; click the rounded bar to expand the step-by-step trace.
  • Leave a green dot on a sidebar conversation after a turn finishes successfully, cleared when you open that conversation. Share a sidebar project across CLIs, peek at its details on hover, and start a new chat on any of them.
  • Let each coding assistant use either the local sign-in or a Nomi-managed account, with optional custom launch commands in advanced settings.
  • Fix new conversations that would not take typing: focus returns to the chat when the built-in browser hides, a stale file preview no longer locks a new chat, and the splash screen no longer swallows clicks.
  • Keep the last user message if the app restarts mid-reply (for example while installing an update). It stays in the chat with a "this turn was interrupted by a restart" card and a Retry button. Queued composer messages and mid-turn steers persist across the restart too.
  • Center the empty-chat home vertically. When no model is available, show a card to add or choose one. Align the light theme and set the workspace background to #FAF9F6.

Details

  • Run Auto mode as each CLI's own judgement instead of guessing support from the model name. Claude's auto mode works again, and Grok now has an Auto tier, so it no longer falls back to asking every time.
  • Fix "Load more" and "Show earlier" doing nothing: local history in the sidebar is no longer reset when the window refocuses, and long chats with large tool traces can keep paging backward.
  • Detect vision support from model metadata only, not from the model name, and fill in built-in prices for mainstream models. Daily Claude Code usage is counted correctly when a custom launcher uses a separate config directory.
  • Harden custom launchers: block command injection in the test command, and restore history scanning, environment passthrough, availability probes and account-source switching.
  • On Windows and Linux, browser-tab windows can no longer send messages to the host page or load the Wails runtime and assets.
  • Show the user's message immediately while context is being compacted or memory is being recalled.
  • Stopped background delegations no longer insert a fake user message into the chat.
  • Open session-details hover cards along the left edge of the pane so they no longer cover the rows below. When the sidebar has many conversations, the sections above the list can be scrolled to and clicked again.
  • Rebuild the subagent hover card: a color status badge, separate Task and Latest output sections, and a full-width open action at the bottom.

v2.3.172026-11-16

Delegated sub-tasks are more dependable: dropped streams and errors retry on their own, and the files they changed come back to the main chat. Click a file mentioned in the chat to open it in the side pane.

  • Resend a step automatically when the model's reply breaks before any tool ran (dropped stream, connection reset, server 5xx, 429 and similar), up to 5 times with growing delays. Auth, quota and context-length errors are not retried.
  • Agents in session details follow live status: a sub-task is listed as running as soon as it appears in the current turn. After an error, continuing in that sub-task shows it running again, then the result of that follow-up. A background sub-agent that is still running after a coding-assistant turn ends keeps its live status.
  • Press ↑ in an empty composer to recall the question you just sent.
  • The session details button now sits next to the button that shows or hides the tab row (4 px apart), so it no longer covers it. On macOS the extra gap of about 40 px is gone. On Windows and Linux it stays to the left of minimize, maximize, and close.
  • The sidebar usage card no longer shows the coding assistant's name; it keeps the colored icon and the same badges. The name is still in the details.
  • Animate the side tabs, the preview pane and the built-in browser when switching and going fullscreen. A sliding indicator moves between tabs, and settings and segmented controls use the same one.
  • Line the sub-task tabs on the right up with the main chat again: in split view the tab row sits back in the title bar, and the conversation top and the composer bottom match the main chat.

Details

  • Agent requests with tools retry 5 times by default, and an unfinished plan that keeps making progress is nudged forward, up to 8 times.
  • A tab whose last task failed is no longer reused for new delegations. Errored or stopped delegation tabs stay open so you can keep replying, and are tidied up after a week idle like other finished tabs. Failed or stopped runs also bring back the files they already edited and name the folder the changes landed in.
  • Follow-up turns in a sub-task and files that already had changes before the delegation are now included in the changes brought back.
  • Agents in session details are grouped by status: running, failed, then done, newest first in each group. Icons and names on tabs, in session details and on hover cards follow the sub-agent's real source.
  • Side chats, open files and preview tabs are remembered per session, and move over once a new coding-assistant tab gets its session.
  • The file tree on the open-file and changes pages can be collapsed, and the choice is remembered.
  • The built-in browser detects pages that refuse to be embedded and pages that never finish loading.
  • File lookup by name skips node_modules, vendor, dist and similar folders.
